preconditions.description: Input integers n (number of teams) and k (number of wins per team against each other team) are within bounds 1 to 1000.
There is at least one team.

postconditions.expression: stdout == '-1' or (all(1 <= int(a) <= n and 1 <= int(b) <= n and int(a) != int(b) for a, b in matches) and len(matches) == m and all(1 <= int(m) <= n * (n - 1) // 2 if n > 1 else 0 for m in [int(stdout.splitlines()[0])]) and all(win_counts[team] == k * (n - 1) for team in range(1, n + 1)))
postconditions.description: If a valid tournament exists, output m (number of matches) followed by m lines of match results (a_i, b_i) where team a_i beats team b_i. Each team must have exactly k wins against every other team. If no valid tournament exists, output -1.

postconditions.expression: stdout == '-1' or (all(win_counts[team] == k * (n - 1) for team in range(1, n + 1)) if n > 1 else True)
postconditions.description: Each team must have exactly k wins against every other team (k*(n-1) total wins). If n=1, no matches are needed.

postconditions.expression: stdout == '-1' or (all(1 <= int(stdout.splitlines()[0]) <= n * (n - 1) // 2 if n > 1 else 0 for _ in [stdout]) and all(int(a) != int(b) for a, b in matches))
postconditions.description: The number of matches m must be between 0 and n*(n-1)/2 (inclusive), and no team plays against itself.
